items.title: Trivial (ring theory)
items.excerpt: 1. A trivial ideal is either the zero or the unit ideal.

items.title: Tensor product algebra (ring theory)
items.excerpt: The tensor product algebra of associative algebras is the tensor product of the algebras as the modules with component multiplication

items.title: Sylvester domain (ring theory)
items.excerpt: A Sylvester domain is a ring in which Sylvester's law of nullity holds.

items.title: Subring (ring theory)
items.excerpt: A subring is a subset S of the ring (R, +, ×) that remains a ring when + and × are restricted to S and contains the multiplicative identity 1 of R.

items.title: Singular submodule (ring theory)
items.excerpt: The right (resp. left) R-module M has a singular submodule if it consists of elements whose annihilators are essential right (resp. left) ideals in R. In set notation it is usually…

items.title: Simple ring (ring theory)
items.excerpt: 1. A simple ring is a non-zero ring that only has trivial two-sided ideals (the zero ideal, the ring itself, and no more) is a simple ring.

items.title: Severi–Brauer variety (ring theory)
items.excerpt: The Severi–Brauer variety is an algebraic variety associated to a given central simple algebra.

items.title: Serial ring (ring theory)
items.excerpt: A right serial ring is a ring that is a right serial module over itself.

items.title: Semisimple ring (ring theory)
items.excerpt: A semisimple ring is an Artinian ring R that is a finite product of simple Artinian rings; in other words, it is a semisimple left R-module.

items.title: Semiprime ring (ring theory)
items.excerpt: 1. A semiprime ring is a ring where the only nilpotent ideal is the trivial ideal {0}. A commutative ring is semiprime if and only if it is reduced.

items.title: Semiprimary ring (ring theory)
items.excerpt: A semiprimary ring is a ring R such that, for the Jacobson radical J(R) of R, (1) R/J(R) is semisimple and (2) J(R) is a nilpotent ideal.

items.title: Semiperfect ring (ring theory)
items.excerpt: A semiperfect ring is a ring R such that, for the Jacobson radical J(R) of R, (1) R/J(R) is semisimple and (2) idempotents lift modulo J(R).

items.title: Self-injective (ring theory)
items.excerpt: A ring R is left self-injective if the module RR is an injective module. While rings with unity are always projective as modules, they are not always injective as modules.

items.title: Radical of an ideal (ring theory)
items.excerpt: The radical of an ideal I in a commutative ring consists of all those ring elements a power of which lies in I. It is equal to the intersection of all prime ideals containing I.

items.title: Quasi-Frobenius ring (ring theory)
items.excerpt: quasi-Frobenius ring: a special type of Artinian ring that is also a self-injective ring on both sides. Every semisimple ring is quasi-Frobenius.

items.title: Perfect (ring theory)
items.excerpt: A left perfect ring is one satisfying the descending chain condition on right principal ideals. They are also characterized as rings whose flat left modules are all projective modu…

items.title: Ore domain (ring theory)
items.excerpt: A left Ore domain is a (non-commutative) domain for which the set of non-zero elements satisfies the left Ore condition. A right Ore domain is defined similarly.

items.title: Order (ring theory)
items.excerpt: An order of an algebra is (roughly) a subalgebra that is also a full lattice.

items.title: Opposite ring (ring theory)
items.excerpt: Given a ring R, its opposite ring Rop has the same underlying set as R, the addition operation is defined as in R, but the product of s and r in Rop is rs, while the product is sr…

items.title: Noetherian ring (ring theory)
items.excerpt: A left Noetherian ring is a ring satisfying the ascending chain condition for left ideals. A right Noetherian is defined similarly and a ring that is both left and right Noetherian…

items.title: Nilpotent (ring theory)
items.excerpt: 1. An element r of R is nilpotent if there exists a positive integer n such that rn = 0.

items.title: Nil ideal (ring theory)
items.excerpt: 1. A nil ideal is an ideal consisting of nilpotent elements.

items.title: Nearring (ring theory)
items.excerpt: A nearring is a structure that is a group under addition, a semigroup under multiplication, and whose multiplication distributes on the right over addition.

items.title: Morita equivalent (ring theory)
items.excerpt: Two rings are said to be Morita equivalent if the category of modules over the one is equivalent to the category of modules over the other.

items.title: Minimal and maximal (ring theory)
items.excerpt: 1. A left ideal M of the ring R is a maximal left ideal (resp. minimal left ideal) if it is maximal (resp. minimal) among proper (resp. nonzero) left ideals. Maximal (resp. minimal…

items.title: Local ring (ring theory)
items.excerpt: 1. A ring with a unique maximal left ideal is a local ring. These rings also have a unique maximal right ideal, and the left and the right unique maximal ideals coincide. Certain c…

items.title: Jacobson radical (ring theory)
items.excerpt: 1. The Jacobson radical of a ring is the intersection of all maximal left ideals.

items.title: Irreducible (ring theory)
items.excerpt: An element x of an integral domain is irreducible if it is not a unit and for any elements a and b such that x = ab, either a or b is a unit. Note that every prime element is irred…

items.title: Invariant basis number (ring theory)
items.excerpt: A ring R has invariant basis number if Rm isomorphic to Rn as R-modules implies m = n.

items.title: Integral domain (ring theory)
items.excerpt: "integral domain" or "entire ring" is another name for a commutative domain; i.e., a nonzero commutative ring with no zero divisors except 0.

items.title: Idempotent (ring theory)
items.excerpt: An element r of a ring is idempotent if r2 = r.

items.title: Hereditary (ring theory)
items.excerpt: A ring is left hereditary if its left ideals are all projective modules. Right hereditary rings are defined analogously.

items.title: Generate (ring theory)
items.excerpt: An associative algebra A over a commutative ring R is said to be generated by a subset S of A if the smallest subalgebra containing S is A itself and S is said to be the generating…

items.title: Free ideal ring (ring theory)
items.excerpt: 1. A free ideal ring or a fir is a ring in which every right ideal is a free module of fixed rank.

items.title: Finitely presented (ring theory)
items.excerpt: A finitely presented algebra over a commutative ring R is a (commutative) associative algebra that is a quotient of a polynomial ring over R in finitely many variables by a finitel…

items.title: Finitely generated (ring theory)
items.excerpt: 1. A left ideal I is finitely generated if there exist finitely many elements a1,..., an such that I = Ra1 +... + Ran. A right ideal I is finitely generated if there exist finitely…

items.title: Filtered ring (ring theory)
items.excerpt: A filtered ring is a ring with a filtration.

items.title: Exterior algebra (ring theory)
items.excerpt: The exterior algebra of a vector space or a module V is the quotient of the tensor algebra of V by the ideal generated by elements of the form x ⊗ x.

items.title: Enveloping algebra (ring theory)
items.excerpt: The (universal) enveloping algebra E of a not-necessarily-associative algebra A is the associative algebra determined by A in some universal way. The best known example is the univ…

items.title: Endomorphism ring (ring theory)
items.excerpt: An endomorphism ring is a ring formed by the endomorphisms of an object with additive structure; the multiplication is taken to be function composition, while its addition is point…

items.title: Division ring (ring theory)
items.excerpt: A division ring or skew field is a ring in which every nonzero element is a unit and 1 ≠ 0.

items.title: Divisor (ring theory)
items.excerpt: 1. In an integral domain R,[clarification needed] an element a is called a divisor of the element b (and we say a divides b) if there exists an element x in R with ax = b.

items.title: Direct product (ring theory)
items.excerpt: A direct product of a family of rings is a ring given by taking the cartesian product of the given rings and defining the algebraic operations component-wise.

items.title: Differential algebra (ring theory)
items.excerpt: A differential algebra is an algebra together with a derivation.

items.title: Derivation (ring theory)
items.excerpt: 1. A derivation of a possibly-non-associative algebra A over a commutative ring R is an R-linear endomorphism that satisfies the Leibniz rule.

items.title: Commutative (ring theory)
items.excerpt: 1. A ring R is commutative if the multiplication is commutative, i.e. rs = sr for all r,s ∈ R.

items.title: Coherent ring (ring theory)
items.excerpt: A left coherent ring is a ring such that every finitely generated left ideal of it is a finitely presented module; in other words, it is coherent as a left module over itself.

items.title: Clifford algebra (ring theory)
items.excerpt: A Clifford algebra is a certain associative algebra that is useful in geometry and physics.

items.title: Change of rings (ring theory)
items.excerpt: A change of rings is a functor (between appropriate categories) induced by a ring homomorphism.

items.title: Characteristic (ring theory)
items.excerpt: 1. The characteristic of a ring is the smallest positive integer n satisfying nx = 0 for all elements x of the ring, if such an n exists. Otherwise, the characteristic is 0.

items.title: Centralizer (ring theory)
items.excerpt: 1. The centralizer of a subset S of a ring is the subring of the ring consisting of the elements commuting with the elements of S. For example, the centralizer of the ring itself i…

items.title: Centre (ring theory)
items.excerpt: 1. An element r of a ring R is central if xr = rx for all x in R. The set of all central elements forms a subring of R, known as the centre of R.

items.title: Brauer group (ring theory)
items.excerpt: The Brauer group of a field is an abelian group consisting of all equivalence classes of central simple algebras over the field.

items.title: Boolean ring (ring theory)
items.excerpt: A boolean ring is a ring in which every element is multiplicatively idempotent.

items.title: Bidimension of an associative algebra (ring theory)
items.excerpt: The bidimension of an associative algebra A over a commutative ring R is the projective dimension of A as an (Aop ⊗R A)-module. For example, an algebra has bidimension zero if and…

items.title: Associate (ring theory)
items.excerpt: In a commutative ring, an element a is called an associate of an element b if a divides b and b divides a.

items.title: Artinian ring (ring theory)
items.excerpt: A left Artinian ring is a ring satisfying the descending chain condition for left ideals; a right Artinian ring is one satisfying the descending chain condition for right ideals. I…

items.title: Amitsur complex (ring theory)
items.excerpt: The Amitsur complex of a ring homomorphism is a cochain complex that measures the extent in which the ring homomorphism fails to be faithfully flat.

items.title: Grothendieck's Galois theory (field theory)
items.excerpt: A very abstract approach from algebraic geometry, introduced to study the analogue of the fundamental group.

items.title: Tensor product of fields (field theory)
items.excerpt: A different foundational piece of algebra, including the compositum operation (join of fields).

items.title: Normal basis (field theory)
items.excerpt: A basis in the vector space sense of L over K, on which the Galois group of L over K acts transitively.

items.title: Artin–Schreier theory (field theory)
items.excerpt: Covers an exceptional case of Kummer theory, in characteristic p.

items.title: Kummer theory (field theory)
items.excerpt: The Galois theory of taking nth roots, given enough roots of unity. It includes the general theory of quadratic extensions.

items.title: Galois group (field theory)
items.excerpt: The automorphism group of a Galois extension. When it is a finite extension, this is a finite group of order equal to the degree of the extension. Galois groups for infinite extens…

items.title: Distinguished class (field theory)
items.excerpt: A class C of field extensions with the three properties[17] If E is a C-extension of F and F is a C-extension of K then E is a C-extension of K. If E and F are C-extensions of K in…

items.title: Totally transcendental extension (field theory)
items.excerpt: An extension E/F such that F is algebraically closed in F.[14]

items.title: Self-regular extension (field theory)
items.excerpt: An extension E/F such that E ⊗F E is an integral domain.[16]

items.title: Simple radical extension (field theory)
items.excerpt: A simple extension E/F generated by a single element α satisfying αn = b for an element b of F. In characteristic p, we also take an extension by a root of an Artin–Schreier polyno…

items.title: Regular extension (field theory)
items.excerpt: An extension E/F such that E is separable over F and F is algebraically closed in E.[12]

items.title: Purely transcendental extension (field theory)
items.excerpt: An extension E/F in which every element of E not in F is transcendental over F.[13][14]

items.title: Primary extension (field theory)
items.excerpt: An extension E/F such that the algebraic closure of F in E is purely inseparable over F; equivalently, E is linearly disjoint from the separable closure of F.[12]

items.title: Simple extension (field theory)
items.excerpt: An extension which is generated by a single element, called a primitive element, or generating element.[9] The primitive element theorem classifies such extensions.[10]

items.title: Frobenius field (field theory)
items.excerpt: A pseudo algebraically closed field whose absolute Galois group has the embedding property.[8]

items.title: Linked field (field theory)
items.excerpt: A field over which no biquaternion algebra is a division algebra.[7]

items.title: CM-field or J-field (field theory)
items.excerpt: An algebraic number field which is a totally imaginary quadratic extension of a totally real field.[6]

items.title: Kroneckerian field (field theory)
items.excerpt: A totally real algebraic number field or a totally imaginary quadratic extension of a totally real field.[5]

items.title: Hilbertian field (field theory)
items.excerpt: A field satisfying Hilbert's irreducibility theorem: formally, one for which the projective line is not thin in the sense of Serre.[3][4]

items.title: Henselian field (field theory)
items.excerpt: A field satisfying Hensel lemma w.r.t. some valuation. A generalization of complete fields.

items.title: Pseudo algebraically closed field (field theory)
items.excerpt: A field in which every variety has a rational point.[2]

items.title: Local field (field theory)
items.excerpt: A completion of some global field (w.r.t. a prime of the integer ring).

items.title: Global field (field theory)
items.excerpt: A number field or a function field of one variable over a finite field.

items.title: Totally real field (field theory)
items.excerpt: A number field generated by a root of a polynomial, having all its roots real numbers.

items.title: Cyclotomic field (field theory)
items.excerpt: An extension of the rational numbers generated by a root of unity.

items.title: Quadratic field (field theory)
items.excerpt: A degree-two extension of the rational numbers.

items.title: Number field (field theory)
items.excerpt: Finite extension of the field of rational numbers.

items.title: Ordered field (field theory)
items.excerpt: A field with a total order compatible with its operations.

items.title: Finite field (field theory)
items.excerpt: A field with finitely many elements, a.k.a. Galois field.

items.title: Field homomorphism (field theory)
items.excerpt: A field homomorphism between two fields E and F is a ring homomorphism, i.e., a function f: E → F

items.title: Transcendence degree (field theory)
items.excerpt: The number of algebraically independent transcendental elements in a field extension. It is used to define the dimension of an algebraic variety.

items.title: Algebraically independent elements (field theory)
items.excerpt: Elements of an extension field of F are algebraically independent over F if they don't satisfy any non-zero polynomial equation with coefficients in F.

items.title: Transcendental (field theory)
items.excerpt: Those elements of an extension field of F that are not algebraic over F are transcendental over F.

items.title: Algebraically closed field (field theory)
items.excerpt: A field F is algebraically closed if every polynomial in F[x] has a root in F; equivalently: every polynomial in F[x] is a product of linear factors.

items.title: Imperfect degree (field theory)
items.excerpt: Let F be a field of characteristic p 0; then Fp is a subfield. The degree [F: Fp] is called the imperfect degree of F. The field F is perfect if and only if its imperfect degree is…

items.title: Perfect field (field theory)
items.excerpt: A field such that every finite extension is separable. All fields of characteristic zero, and all finite fields, are perfect.

items.title: Separable extension (field theory)
items.excerpt: An extension generated by roots of separable polynomials.

items.title: Normal extension (field theory)
items.excerpt: A field extension generated by the complete factorisation of a set of polynomials.

items.title: Splitting field (field theory)
items.excerpt: A field extension generated by the complete factorisation of a polynomial.

items.title: Primitive element (field theory)
items.excerpt: An element α of an extension field E over a field F is called a primitive element if E=F(α), the smallest extension field containing α. Such an extension is called a simple extensi…

items.title: Generating set (field theory)
items.excerpt: Given a field extension E/F and a subset S of E, we write F(S) for the smallest subfield of E that contains both F and S. It consists of all the elements of E that can be obtained…

items.title: Algebraic extension (field theory)
items.excerpt: If an element α of an extension field E over F is the root of a non-zero polynomial in F[x], then α is algebraic over F. If every element of E is algebraic over F, then E/F is an a…
